title: Geometry of the Sacred
subtitle: A Thermodynamic & Topological Map of Soul, Heaven, Hell, Karma & Mysticism

blocks.text: This chapter presents the poster “Geometry of the Sacred” in full. It is a single dense diagram; open it, then use the explanation, read-aloud, and Ask-AI tools beneath it to work through the ideas at your own pace.

blocks.caption: Figure 22.1 — Geometry of the Sacred: A Thermodynamic & Topological Map of Soul, Heaven, Hell, Karma & Mysticism.
blocks.explanation: The companion sheet to the spiritual phenomenology poster, organized as five parts with a comparative panel across four traditions. Part 1 treats the soul as the irreducible, non-computable centre of the Markov blanket — the singularity of awareness that observes the generative model — and sets Sanatan Dharma's Atman, Islam's Tawheed and Ruh, Christianity's Pneuma with Agape as the trajectory-defining force, and Buddhism's Anatta side by side as four readings of that same position, the last denying the singularity outright. Part 2 gives heaven and hell as terminal attractor states of the cognitive and spiritual manifold. Part 3 reads karma through the Gita as topological and informational conservation, with karmic debt as structural friction forcing re-instantiation until equilibrium is reached, and Nishkama Karma as the zero-friction geodesic to liberation. Part 4 separates religion as the laws of the manifold from mysticism as the laboratory for altering its topology, with prayer, meditation, ethics and devotion as daily metric-smoothing operations. Part 5 places the Nasadiya Suktam at zero-point: no space, no time, no observer, pure symmetry and zero entropy, broken by the first perturbation.
blocks.tts: The geometry of the sacred. Topology is theology, thermodynamics is dharma — different languages, one manifold, one truth.
